precepts.text: In the days of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves. That is the first time Esau broke the yoke from off his neck, just as Genesis 27:40 prophesied.
precepts.point: And shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck. When did that first happen?
precepts.why:
Esau cried, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” Jacob had already received the major blessing. Rebekah sent him in, dressed in goats' hair so he would feel hairy like his brother, because she remembered what God told her at the birth: the elder shall serve the younger. When Jacob feared a curse, she said let it fall on her. The white man's the devil, and when you ask the Christians about those two boys, they say Jacob was the evil son and Esau the good one, and black people in church echo those same sentiments. No: Jacob was the good one. Esau was the profane one, the fornicator, the one who despised his birthright, and Rebekah was being obedient to God.

Isaac answered Esau: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” Dew falls everywhere, and wherever it falls, Esau would live; he would have the best places on the planet. How would he get them? “And by thy sword shalt thou live”: by war. God through Isaac blessed Esau with the art of war, the same blessing Cain's line had when Tubal-cain made all kinds of weapons.

Then: “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” When did that first happen? 2 Kings 8 answers. “Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign”, and “he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of the Lord.” Yet the Lord would not destroy Judah for David's sake. “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” That is the first time Esau broke the yoke from off his neck, just as Genesis 27:40 prophesied.

After that, Edom turned on his brother outright. When the Babylonians destroyed the first temple in 586 BCE, Edom helped them instead of helping Judah: rejoicing, looting the city, blocking the survivors who fled. Obadiah, “concerning Edom”, says, “even thou wast as one of them”, and “Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape.” 1 Esdras names who set the fire: “the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.”

precepts.text: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves: the breaking of the yoke the blessing spoke of.
precepts.point: And it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck: that happened in the days of the kings, and we went back and forth; there was dominion again in 193 AD under Septimius Severus, and it was lost again around the Renaissance. So Esau is going to have possession of the earth, and he is going to kill to get it.
precepts.why:
Isaac told Esau, “Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants.” Jacob was made Esau’s lord; the elder would serve the younger. Everybody on this planet was meant to be our servants. It is our birthright; we are the rulers of this earth. But the only way to get it back is to remember where we fell off and what we did wrong, and Christianity will not teach us that. It keeps us in the wrong, and keeps us divided into Adventist, Protestant, Pentecostal, Mormon and Jehovah’s Witness, with none of them telling us who we are.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept,” and he still got a blessing: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.” The best portions of the earth, and the dew that falls on the whole earth. But the whole earth was already given to Jacob. How the hell is Esau going to get the best part of the earth? The next words answer it: “by thy sword shalt thou live.” He would take it by the sword. He is a killer, yet wherever he goes he says he comes in peace, that he only wants to liberate the people and bring them freedom, while it is missiles after missiles, rape after rape, nothing but atrocities once he is let in. That's what democracy is about: now you could be a homo, nobody can judge you; now you could be a transgender, nobody can judge you. The book of Maccabees shows evil multiplying on the earth when they took control.

The blessing ends, “and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.” 2 Kings 8:20 shows that yoke breaking: “In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” Edom had served Judah, and in the days of the kings he threw it off.

From there it went back and forth. There was dominion again in 193 AD under Septimius Severus, wicked as hell as it was, and it was lost again around the Renaissance. So Isaac’s words have come to pass: Esau has possession of the earth, and he killed to get it.

precepts.text: Isaac tells Esau he will serve his brother but will break the yoke when he gains the dominion.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

precepts.why:
Isaac told Esau, “Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants”. Esau lifted up his voice and wept for a blessing, and Isaac answered, “by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.”

Edom is Esau. From the days of David and Solomon, Edom had been in subjection to Judah, serving his brother. Then in Jehoram’s days “Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.” Joram went over to Zair and smote the Edomites that compassed him about, “Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day.”

That revolt is the word spoken to Esau fulfilled: when he gained the dominion, he broke the yoke from off his neck. It is a pattern that reaches all the way to Edom’s later rise.

points: Another wicked woman that used the men around her to manipulate the people of Israel: Athaliah. Her son Ahaziah reigned one year in Jerusalem, and he walked in the way of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab.

points: Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: The timing is of the Most High, so the king restores all that was hers and the fruits of the field from the day she left.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Elisha tells Hazael the king may recover but the Most High has shown that he shall surely die, then weeps because he sees the evil Hazael will do to Israel: burning strongholds, slaying young men, and ripping up women with child.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the kings of Israel because the daughter of Ahab was his wife.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: He does evil in the sight of the Most High, yet Judah is not destroyed for David his servant's sake, according to the promise.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: In Jehoram's days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah and makes a king over itself, breaking the subjection Edom had been under from the days of David and Solomon.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Jehoram sleeps with his fathers and is buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Ahaziah son of Jehoram begins to reign over Judah and walks in the way of the house of Ahab, being the son-in-law of that house, a picture of the generational curse passed from father to son.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: He goes with Jehoram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria, and the Syrians wound Jehoram at Ramah.
Jehoram returns to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah goes down to see him, setting the stage for both kings to meet Jehu's judgment.
